newsitem.title: INDIA: Evacuations begin as cyclone nears Indian coast.
newsitem.headline: Evacuations begin as cyclone nears Indian coast.

text.p: Authorities began evacuating thousands of people on Wednesday from coastal areas of India's southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh as a powerful cyclone moved closer to land.

"We have already evacuated about 75,000 people from low-lying coastal areas," state relief commissioner H.S Brahma told Reuters. "We will continue the evacuations till we are sure there is no danger."

The cyclone, with winds of 150-180 kmh (94-113 miles per hour), was expected to hit the state's coast shortly after noon on Wednesday, officials said. It would be the second in a month to hit the coastal state.
The storm would send tidal waves two to three metres high (six to nine feet) surging up to 10 kilometres (six miles) inland, officials said.
At 5:30 a.m. (0000 GMT), the storm was around 200 km (125 miles) southeast of the coastal town of Machilipatnam, an official at the storm warning centre at Visakhapatnam told Reuters.
"The cyclone will hit land shortly after noon if it maintains its present speed," he said. "It is likely to cross the coast between (the coastal towns of) Ongole and Kakinada."

Officials in the state capital Hyderabad said they feared the cyclone would cause more damage than the one which devastated coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh state on November 6 and 7. That storm generated winds of up to 220 kmh (138 mph).
More than 2,000 people were killed or lost at sea in the storm which caused damage to crops and property worth more than 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion).
C.V.V. Bhadram, meteorological centre director at Hyderabad, said the coastal areas were already overcast and lashed by rain.
"The coastal areas witnessed light rains in the night and will experience heavy rains from now on," he said. "The coast is being lashed by winds of 60-70 kmh (38-44 mph).
Officials said they feared widespread damage from the gale-force winds. They said they expected power cables to be snapped, trees to be uprooted and communications lines to be cut.

Traffic along the east coast between Vijayawada town and Madras, capital of the adjoining state of Tamil Nadu was expected to be hit. Officials said they expected overhead electric traction wires to be snapped and rail tracks to be washed away.

On Tuesday, cyclone warnings were issued along the coast and fishermen were warned not to put out to sea. The armed forces had been placed on alert to assist civilian authorities in relief operations, officials said.
In November 1977, a cyclone killed more than 10,000 people in the Diviseema region near Machilipatnam in the same state.
